title: collectReward(1) permissionless griefing: any wallet can re-anchor rewardPerSecond at trivial cost, extending the already-broken V1 depletion tail indefinitely
rootCause: `collectReward` is permissionless (no access control beyond `nonReentrant`), accepts any `amount > 0`, and ends by recomputing `rewardPerSecond = (rewardBalance * PRECISION) / depletionDuration`. Combined with the V1 `_updatePool` re-anchor (DEDUP-001), any third party pinging `collectReward(1)` periodically can keep `rewardPerSecond` clamped near zero indefinitely.
impactSummary: Reward token effectively never reaches stakers in the advertised depletionDuration. Worse than DEDUP-001's baseline asymptotic behavior because a griefer with a tiny budget can mechanically reset the rate every block.
preservedDetails: CODE-008 carries the full attack walkthrough (1 wei per block, sub-cent total cost on L2). Distinct from CODE-001/DEDUP-001 because it adds the permissionless-amplification angle on top of the known V1 bug.
remediation: Gate `collectReward` to the trusted stable-yield-accumulator (natspec already names the expected caller); or enforce a minimum funding amount; the deeper fix is the V2 change (no rate recompute inside `_updatePool`).
dedupNotes: Conceptually nested under DEDUP-001 but kept as separate finding because (a) DEDUP-001 is matches-known-issue and will be suppressed; this is a fresh amplification surface, (b) different remediation (access control vs rate-freeze refactor). Note however that the underlying V1 bug is documented known-issue; the sanitizer should preserve THIS finding (the permissionless amplifier) while suppressing DEDUP-001 (the underlying bug).
relatedFindings: DEDUP-009 (ECON-003 funder-vs-staker symmetry on collectReward MEV)
